title: Coherent-State Integrals Beyond the Domain of Operator Products
abstract: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain $e^{μa^2}e^{λa^{\dagger2}}$ of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a rigorous method to evaluate matrix elements of complex operator products in quantum systems by comparing the results from three distinct mathematical frameworks: the direct operator product, the coherent-state integral, and the Fock-space series. The core finding is that the coherent-state integral acts as an analytic continuation, providing meaningful results even when the direct product or the series expansion fails to converge. This is crucial for extending quantum calculations into previously inaccessible parameter regimes.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to calculate matrix elements of products of unbounded quantum operators, specifically involving two-photon exponentials, when the product is not mathematically defined in the standard sense.
main_result: The coherent-state integral provides an analytic continuation of the matrix element, allowing calculations in parameter regimes where the operator product or the standard Fock-space series diverge.
method: The analysis compares three mathematical formulations—the operator product, the coherent-state integral, and the Fock-space series—using a resolution of the identity and establishing a hierarchy of convergence regions.
model_or_system: The system involves single-mode bosonic operators ($a, a^\dagger$) and their associated two-photon exponentials, relevant to quantum optics and squeezing phenomena.
key_observables: The convergence and existence of the product in different mathematical senses (vector, sesquilinear form, integral, series).
important_parameters: The complex parameters $\lambda$ and $\mu$ defining the two-photon exponentials, which determine the five distinct parameter regions of validity.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a weak composition lemma and assumes the validity of the resolution of the identity for the chosen operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the five parameter regions in the complex $\lambda-\mu$ plane, showing the nested and overlapping domains of validity for the different mathematical formulations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the strong identity, the product as a vector, the product as a form, the integral, and the series, demonstrating that the integral carries the analytic continuation across the failure domains of the others.
why_interesting: It provides advanced mathematical tools for handling non-standard operator products in quantum field theory and quantum optics, extending physical calculations beyond naive convergence criteria.
